messages.subject: OccuPEN_CV Model Selection and predict()
parts:
Hi all,

This group has been exceptionally helpful so far from all the past conversations, but alas I have finally encountered something that I cannot find an answer to in previous conversations. 

I am working with a relatively small dataset using single season occupancy (n=204 with 66 observations) that had been giving me issues in terms of parameter estimates and SE's. The more complex models were producing a great amount of boundary estimates and this was an issue since I am more concerned with inference gained from parameters in my study than predictions back to the site levels. I recently looked into the occuPEN_CV method of model fitting and it appears that most of my issues have been resolved (better estimates, more what I expected considering the biology of my intended species). I have read the Hutchinson et al. 2015 paper and from their results, I plan to use the 'Ridge' penalty type since this method most often found estimates closest to the true values.

My question is how to go about model selection with this procedure. From what I have read it appears that AICc should no longer be used since this is already a form of penalized likelihood. I have seen recommendations of using the highest cross-validated score to compare models, with the highest score being the most supported. This makes sense since more complex models are likely to impose a greater penalty, making straight AIC comparison biased. I have seen the recent code posted to assess the CV scores in occuMulti(), but I am wondering how I could apply this approach with an unmarkedFitOccuPEN_CV object. Any assistance would be greatly appreciated.

Another question is how to obtain SE's and CI's for the predict() function using this method of model fitting. I have followed recommendations to use nonparboot to obtain SE's of the paramters in the model, but I am unsure of how to either bind these to the fitted model object to use predict normally or add these as an additional argument in the call to predict(). Again, any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks!

Aaron
